significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds, and more is true: for every odd k = 2m+1 the Sprague–Grundy value of the empty board of length n is (n + [n mod (3m+2) ≥ k]) mod 2. With P = 3m+2, either player can force the game to end with exactly 2⌊n/P⌋ + [n mod P ≥ k] empty cells, even when one extra nim-heap of size one is added: the board is cut into blocks of k + (m+1) cells, each containing m+1 disjoint supports and only m high cells, and the defender answers inside the block the opponent just played in. So the length of the game is fixed and its parity gives the value; the bound G ≤ 1 and both identities follow from the formula. Lean defines the game on the sets of unmarked cells (a position is legal when every window of k cells contains an unmarked cell), the options and the Sprague–Grundy value as a minimum excluded value, proves the three statements of the conjecture and the closed formula for every m ≥ 0, and proves that the moves of this model are, move for move, the placements of the source's game on a Boolean board.
significance.caveat: The source prints no range for a; the translation identity is proved for every a ≥ 0 and the reflection identity for 0 ≤ a ≤ 5m+2, the range in which both boards exist (Lean also covers the degenerate m = 0). Lean works with the sets of unmarked cells; the match with the source's board is kernel-checked move for move, and the equality of Sprague–Grundy values on the two models follows by a short induction that is not a separate Lean theorem. The argument is short and elementary (one page); the source's authors proved only k = 3, by a longer method, and wrote that their method is insufficient for general odd k. This is the second counted result from arXiv:2604.16759 after 374250, a different conjecture (Section 5.1, one-piece positions at k = 3) proved by a different method; neither follows from the other. No journal version of the source is known. All work is by AI and no human has checked it: the proof, the Lean code and the paper are by GPT-6.2 Sol lanes; the adversarial review before Lean (not routine 0.75) and the final check (not routine 0.70) are by two separate Claude Opus 5.5 lanes. The Semantic Scholar citation list was rate-limited; OpenAlex was used for citations.
